inputs.ground_truth_sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.status FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.type = 'Artifact' AND T2.format = 'vintage' AND T1.side IS NULL
inputs.predicted_sql:
SELECT c.name, l.status
FROM cards c
JOIN legalities l ON c.uuid = l.uuid
WHERE c.type ILIKE '%artifact%'
  AND (c.otherfaceids IS NULL OR c.otherfaceids = '')
  AND l.format = 'vintage'

    FROM transactions_1k t

)

    c.customerid,

Many of us use linear regression in rough-and-ready fashion to learn about the relative importance of predictors, to assess the shape of relationships, and so on. But if one wants to make strict probabilistic inferences one needs to satisfy the set of standard assumptions entailed in such regression. The most important of these are random sampling and independent observations. Another one is that the regression residuals (not any particular X or Y variable) should be normally distributed. Without satisfying all of the standard assumptions, one cannot vouch for the accuracy of standard errors or p-values.

JOIN drivers d ON r_current.driverid = d.driverid

    ORDER BY r2.raceid

WITH english_major AS (
    SELECT
        c.Code,
        c.Name,
        c.Population,
        c.SurfaceArea,
        c.Population / c.SurfaceArea AS density
    FROM country c
    JOIN countrylanguage cl ON c.Code = cl.CountryCode
    WHERE cl.Language = 'English' AND cl.Percentage > 50
)
SELECT
    maxc.Name AS CountryWithHighestDensity,
    (maxc.density / minc.density) AS TimesLargerThanLowest
FROM
    (SELECT * FROM english_major ORDER BY density DESC LIMIT 1) AS maxc
CROSS JOIN
    (SELECT * FROM english_major ORDER BY density ASC LIMIT 1) AS minc

inputs.question: If life expectancy increases by 10 years in countries with per capita GNP greater than the average per capita GNP of all European countries, what is the expected year of death for people born in the year of Zambia's independence asccording to Zambia's life expectancy?
inputs.ground_truth_sql: SELECT CAST ( IndepYear + LifeExpectancy AS INT ) AS death_year FROM ( SELECT name , IndepYear , LifeExpectancy + 10 AS LifeExpectancy FROM country WHERE 1.0 * GNP / Population > ( SELECT 1.0 * SUM ( GNP ) / SUM ( Population ) FROM country WHERE Continent = "Europe" ) UNION ALL SELECT name , IndepYear , LifeExpectancy FROM country WHERE NOT ( 1.0 * GNP / Population > ( SELECT 1.0 * SUM ( GNP ) / SUM ( Population ) FROM country WHERE Continent = "Europe" ) ) ) WHERE name = "Zambia"
inputs.predicted_sql:
SELECT
  c.Name,
  c.IndepYear,
  c.LifeExpectancy,
  (c.GNP / c.Population) AS PerCapitaGNP,
  (SELECT AVG(GNP / Population) FROM country WHERE Continent = 'Europe') AS AvgEuropePerCapitaGNP,
  CASE WHEN (c.GNP / c.Population) > (SELECT AVG(GNP / Population) FROM country WHERE Continent = 'Europe')
       THEN c.LifeExpectancy + 10
       ELSE c.LifeExpectancy
  END AS AdjustedLifeExpectancy,
  (c.IndepYear + CASE WHEN (c.GNP / c.Population) > (SELECT AVG(GNP / Population) FROM country WHERE Continent = 'Europe')
                     THEN c.LifeExpectancy + 10
                     ELSE c.LifeExpectancy
  END) AS ExpectedYearOfDeath
FROM country c
WHERE c.Name = 'Zambia';

inputs.predicted_sql:
WITH win_counts AS (
    SELECT winner_name,
           COUNT(*) AS win_count,
           MAX(winner_rank_points) AS rank_points
    FROM matches
    GROUP BY winner_name
)
SELECT winner_name AS name,
       rank_points
FROM win_counts
ORDER BY win_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
